The IRS has 10 years to collect a tax debt. The clock starts when the tax is assessed, and each assessment has its own date.
Some things pause that clock: a payment plan request, an offer in compromise, a Collection Due Process hearing, bankruptcy, or living outside the U.S. for 6 months or more.
This one-page guide shows what pauses it and for how long, with the official sources.

Lien or levy? They are not the same.
A lien is the government's legal claim against your property. A levy actually takes it: wages, bank accounts, even your car or house.
Before a levy, the IRS usually sends a Final Notice of Intent to Levy at least 30 days ahead. That notice also tells you about your right to a hearing. Act before the deadline on your letter.

See the full infographic: https://getirshelp.com/blog/irs-lien-vs-levy-infographic/
Questions? Call tax attorney Darrin Mish at (813) 229-7100.

Can't pay the IRS? You have options.
A payment plan lets you pay over time. An offer in compromise settles the debt for less than the full amount, if you qualify. Currently Not Collectible status temporarily delays most collection until your finances improve.
Each one fits a different situation. This guide shows how the IRS describes each option and who it fits.

See the full infographic: https://getirshelp.com/blog/cant-pay-irs-three-options-infographic/

Is that call, email or text really from the IRS?
The IRS says it isn't if it comes out of the blue, rushes you, threatens arrest, asks for personal or financial information, or demands payment now.
First contact from the IRS is normally a letter by U.S. mail. A social media direct message is never from the IRS.

See the full infographic: https://getirshelp.com/blog/is-it-really-the-irs-scam-red-flags-infographic/
Questions? Call tax attorney Darrin Mish at (813) 229-7100.

fbli:
Can bankruptcy wipe out income tax? Sometimes.
The timing tests, counted back from the day you file bankruptcy: the return was due more than 3 years before, a late return was filed more than 2 years before, and the IRS assessed the tax more than 240 days before. Each tax year is tested on its own.
Meeting the timing tests does not guarantee a discharge. Have your transcripts reviewed before you file.

See the full infographic: https://getirshelp.com/blog/bankruptcy-income-tax-3-2-240-infographic/
Questions? Call tax attorney Darrin Mish at (813) 229-7100.

Who gets audited? For tax year 2021, the IRS had examined or was examining 0.3% of individual returns.
The rate was 0.2% for incomes from $25,000 to under $500,000, 1.8% for returns with no total positive income, and 6.6% for incomes of $10 million or more.
The numbers come straight from the IRS Data Book.
